OMA-URI Atlas

Every node Microsoft's DDF files declare, drawn as the management tree the MDM client walks. Search for a node or open a branch; the highlighter traces its OMA-URI from ./ to the node, and the panel shows what the DDF says about it: the verbs it allows, its format and values, and which Windows builds and editions it applies to.

./{Device | User | —}/Vendor/MSFT/{CSP}/{nodes…}  ·  ./{DevInfo | DevDetail | SyncML}/…

Management tree

Select a node to open it; select it again to fold it. Long lists scroll with the page.

    • folded
    • open, or a leaf
    • {name} you create
    • path segment no DDF declares
    • OMA-URI of the selected node

    Source: Microsoft's DDF v2 files, DDFv2Feb2026.zip (). Descriptions are the DDF's own, shortened. Build names and anchors come from the matching Microsoft Learn pages; a Learn link opens the node's own section when Learn has one. Edition names are decoded from the Windows PRODUCT_* constants.

    Scope: Learn documents 93 CSPs; Microsoft's DDF drops cover 52 of them, and this atlas draws exactly those. CSPs with no published DDF, such as Update, WindowsAutopilot, Win32AppInventory and TenantLockdown, are not here. Learn's applicability tables list only Pro, Enterprise, Education and IoT Enterprise; where the DDF also allows Home or Windows SE, the panel says so. Where the DDF and Learn disagree, the panel marks it DDF vs Learn.
